notes: Extracted 29 October 2026 from the guide (src/guides/toggle.guide.tsx) and docs/evidence/toggle.md at 889444e (“docs: publish the #194–#211 Coin fixes to their guides”, 13 October), the same files on main and docs-next. The guide's Sources note was checked on 13 October 2026 on the build it calls the 12 October build (mirror v0.1.78-c1fa197, Biscuit's main at c1fa197, the #209 fix), so items citing it carry 2026-10-13 and 0.1.78-c1fa197. The evidence has three checks: 1 October on 0.1.77 (Figma, Storybook, the props, and the browser measurements), 8 October on 636f3f5 (#181 fixed, #209 found, the shared disabled grey) and 13 October on c1fa197 (#209 fixed). Only the 8 and 13 October sections are cited, with their own dates and builds; the 1 October section (0.1.77) is not cited, and what it says is read against the installed source instead. Installed build: jfs-components 0.1.78, mirror v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (Biscuit's main at dbe0e02, 27 October). GitHub's compare of v0.1.78-c1fa197 and v0.1.78-dbe0e02 (6 commits, 293 files, complete) touches no Toggle file, no design-tokens or resolver file, and no web-platform-utils or shadow util (src/utils changes only web-focus-trap); 636f3f5 to c1fa197 changed only Toggle.tsx's keyboard handling (Space in its own handler, activationKeys 'space') and web-platform-utils, the #209 fix. Installed Toggle.tsx matches every guide and evidence sentence used here, read from source, not run, with token values through the package's own getVariableByName: the track is toggle/width 52 with toggle/padding/track 3 around a toggle/thumb/size 25 thumb, so 52 × 31 (lines 59–72, 83–92), with no size prop; the background is rgb(199,199,204) Off and rgb(93,0,181) On, and rgb(224,224,229) for both Disabled Off and Disabled On, with a rgb(245,245,247) thumb and no shadow when disabled (tokens, Toggle States set by the component); the thumb sits at flex-start when off and flex-end when on (line 90); disabled sets opacity 0.5 (line 91), ignores presses (75, 123) and on the web sets aria-disabled and tabIndex −1 (110–117); value makes it controlled, defaultValue (false) uncontrolled, and onValueChange receives the next value once per press (50–52, 74–81); Space is handled by useKeyboardNavigation with activationKeys 'space' (107–109) and Enter and click by the Pressable; the root is role switch with accessibilityState checked and disabled, aria-checked on the web, and accessibilityLabel as its name (120–128). It has no label prop, no children, no testID and no rest props. No guide sentence used here is contradicted. accessibilityLabel: the accessibility item rests on its type description only (its label for screen readers); every example names the toggle with its row's title, as the guide's own Row does. On the web the row's visible title does not name the switch (no aria-labelledby; its name is aria-label from accessibilityLabel), so the 1 October evidence's report that Storybook asks for the label only “when there is no adjacent visible label” is not recorded. Two notes on wording: the Anatomy description's “the thumb slides right” is read as the thumb's position; the package doesn't animate it (alignItems flips, Toggle.tsx line 90; no Animated in any build from 0.1.77 to dbe0e02), so the entry records positions, not motion, and that sentence is not quoted. The configuration description's “it always sits at the end of a row whose title names the setting” is the guide's pattern for a settings row: Toggle has no label prop, and the Sources note says the screen names it “usually with the row’s title”, so it is recorded as recommended placement with a contextual scope. Modes: the facts list two collections, Color Mode and Toggle States. Toggle States is not a choice: the component sets it itself from value and disabled (Toggle.tsx lines 54–57, after any modes passed in), so a Toggle States mode has no effect; the evidence says so only in its 1 October section (0.1.77), so it is kept here and not added as an evidence fact. No guide sentence gives a mode for any content. useInstead: the Don't “Wait for a Save button” says “use a Checkbox”, so useInstead is Checkbox, the export the guide names (CheckboxItem, which has an entry, is a row with a checkbox; the guide doesn't name it); “Use a pair of Radios” gives Radio, as Slider's entry does for “Radios”. Neither Checkbox nor Radio has an entry in this release. Anatomy: Track and Thumb are always drawn; Off position is the thumb's place while off, so not always present. Content good keeps the guide's three setting names; bad keeps the two words the Content description says not to write. States are the guide's three cards; Disabled is the package's (Figma has no disabled variant). Examples follow the building rules: no Color Mode (the guide sets Light on every component), no modes, no style (the guide's width 100% host is a docs frame). The In context example is the guide's settings card, a Card with a VStack of three horizontal ListItems, each with navArrow off, no support text and a Toggle in trailing named with the row's title, as the guide's own Row does (lines 11–16); the literal values and the empty onValueChange stand for the screen's state and its saving, which the guide says the screen owns. The second example is the guide's Title and support text row. Card, VStack and ListItem have entries (ListItem's is undocumented: facts only; layout Horizontal is needed for trailing, and showSupportText false hides its default “Support Text”). Left out of examples: the bare Off, On and Disabled cards, the Anatomy and Sizing specimens, the Do & Don't pairs (the Save button, the bare pair, the Light / Dark row) and the playground. Not recorded: style (the building rules keep style overrides off Coin components); Dark mode (the guide shows Light only); Figma's variable names and hex values; the Storybook story list. Gaps: the Sources note's own Figma and package difference (Figma has Off and On only; disabled is the package's); and the 8 October evidence's open point that Disabled On and Disabled Off share one grey track, which is how Coin's Toggle tokens define both disabled modes (the same on dbe0e02). Sorting (batch 11): two cross-check runs, no flags. Round 1 noted that /accessibility/1 (“Set accessibilityLabel…”) read as an instruction while its fact only says what the prop is: reworded to the fact (“accessibilityLabel is the toggle's label for screen readers.”), and round 2 ran on that final entry. Both rounds noted that the Sources note's “12 October build” may be 13 October: it isn't a guide error (the mirror build v0.1.78-c1fa197 was made on 12 October, 14:40 UTC, and installed with the 13 October release). Round 2 noted that /facts/gaps/0 carries 13 October while its content was first measured on 1 October: the gap cites the guide's own Sources note, checked 13 October on c1fa197, and Toggle and its tokens are unchanged from there to dbe0e02. No trace-check flags remain. Refreshed 29 October 2026 for guide fix #543 (3f56271): the Track note now says the track is fully rounded; /anatomy/0 quotes the new sentence.

examples.purpose: A settings card, the guide's In context: a Card holding three rows, each a horizontal ListItem whose title names the setting, with no support text and no arrow, and a Toggle at its end named with the same words. Each change applies as soon as the toggle moves; the screen keeps the values and saves them. The literal values and the empty onValueChange stand for the screen's own state and saving.

evidenceFacts.name: value
evidenceFacts.description: On the web, aria-checked follows the value.
evidenceFacts.quote: `aria-checked` follows the value, and Space switches a focused toggle.

evidenceFacts.name: onValueChange
evidenceFacts.description: Called once with the new value for each Enter, Space or click.
evidenceFacts.quote: one Enter calls `onValueChange(true)` once and `aria-checked` becomes `true`; one Space calls it once. Click is unchanged.

evidenceFacts.name: disabled
evidenceFacts.description: On the web, sets aria-disabled and tabindex -1, so Tab skips it.
